newsitem.title: JAPAN: Teijin aims at 37 bln yen parent profit in 2000/01.
newsitem.headline: Teijin aims at 37 bln yen parent profit in 2000/01.

text.p: Teijin Ltd said on Wednesday it is aiming at a parent current profit of 37 billion yen and a group net profit of 36 billion yen in the year to March 31, 2001.

In its latest mid- and long-term plan business plan, the synthetic fibre manufacturer also said it set a target for a group net profit of 45 billion yen and a parent current profit of 50 billion yen in 2005/06.
Teijin posted a group net profit of 8.49 billion yen and a parent current profit of 19.35 billion yen in 1995/96.
Teijin said it is aiming at parent sales of 370 billion yen and group sales of 770 billion yen in 2000/01 and parent sales of 450 billion yen and group sales of 950 billion yen in 2005/06.
In 1995/96 its parent sales stood at 323.37 billion yen and group sales at 618.65 billion yen.

To achieve the projected profits and sales, the company plans to expand its overseas business in polyester fibre and plastic film and to increase its health care business, including sales of drugs and leasing of medical equipment, a Teijin spokesman said.
It also wants to raise sales of synthetic leather and of materials for liquid crystal displays, he said.
Teijin will spend a total of 148 billion yen on group research in the five years to 2000/01, and will spend 194 billion yen on group investment in same period.

It will increase its group work force to 18,500 people by 2000/01 from 16,200 in 1995/96, for its overseas business expansion, while the number of employees at the parent firm will fall to 5,600 by 2000/01 from 6,700 in 1995/96 through natural attrition, the spokesman said.
